Abstract.AbstractText: We present a simple method for the fabrication of colloidal capsules of different sizes ranging from below 100 nm up to one micron. The capsules are produced by self-assembling 5 nm gold nanoparticles at the interface of oil-in-water emulsion droplets. The size of the capsules is regulated by tuning the wetting properties of the nanoparticles by changing either the composition of their ligand shell or the composition of the oil phase. The modified wettability affects not only the size but also the thickness of capsule walls. The wall can be thin if it is made of a single layer of the nanoparticles or thick when composed of multilayers. The durability of such capsules is quite high, although it can be improved by chemical cross-linking with UV light. Such capsules have low permeability, so they can store a molecular cargo and then release it on demand.
